articleTitle: Users' bandwidth needs versus 155.520 Mbit/s broadband interface
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Concerning the future B-ISDN, the bandwidth need of different economic sectors for a B-ISDN access is analysed and the impact on its access network is discussed. For that purpose broadband applications are investigated with respect to important traffic characteristics. It is shown, that more than 50% of the business users will cope with an ATM access capacity of less than 45 Mbit/s. In addition, an easy procedure to obtain traffic patterns for business users is presented.

articleTitle: Lessons learnt from the Bishop's Stortford optical trial
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The objectives and implementation of the wide ranging fibre trial at Bishop's Stortford in the UK are described. The valuable output from the key process of evaluation is highlighted, indicating how this is helping to lead to a positive future for fibre deployment in the UK local access network.

articleTitle: Outline and introduction scenarios of an ATM based optical access network as a service platform
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper describes the "Service Platform" concept as the infrastructure for the local network and its migration scenario in existing situation. By employing ATM technologies and Multi-CLAD in access networks, very flexible and simple local networks can be achieved even in STM (Synchronous Transfer Mode) environments. Moreover, they will evolve very smoothly to the future broadband network.

articleTitle: Design considerations of distributed broadband subscriber access network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Public networks can provide high-speed switching and transmission capabilities. However, a broadband subscriber access network (B-SAN) is needed to provide service integration, various connection types, and to support intelligent tele-services. In this paper, we investigate the B-SAN especially for accommodating the multi-party/multi-point multiple connection and distribution services. We first review the role of distributed B-SAN in comparison with the private- or public-domain MANS. We study the design objectives including bandwidth, connectivity, interface, OAM, and performance. As the results, we summarize the overall design requirements of the distributed B-SAN in the harmony of broadband backbone network and the forthcoming customer premises network (CPN).

articleTitle: Integrated broadband access
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: In recent years, the customer access network has witnessed a rapid development of new transport technologies. Especially, the development of Passive Optical Networks and High speed Digital Subscriber Loop technologies may have a large impact, as they provide cost effective means for gradual introduction of new services in the access network. At the same time, a series of new services and applications are maturing. Computer and consumer industry have discovered multimedia (eg. CD-1). Video distribution services are evolving to fully interactive Video On Demand (VOD, dial tone video) capabilities. These applications need a bandwidth of at least 1.5 Mbit/s. The precise bandwidth requirements are, however, yet unknown. Both multimedia terminals and VOD set-top units will be available and low cost in the short future. For the transport of these video related service, the operator has basically the choice between twisted pair, coax, fiber and radio based access networks, or any combination of the rn. Most access networks today are largely copper based, but fiber is gradually being introduced to cope with the increasing bandwidth demands. In this paper, an access network is described that is capable of mixing these different transport media at different bit rates, using a common multiplexing / concentration scheme. Therefore, it can easily adapt to the multitude of local access topologies cun-ently in use. At the same time, it provides the necessary bandwidth flexibility to support the new services in an efficient way. The system is called Integrated Broadband Access (IBA), as it provides a common access platform for all services, narrowband and broadband, and as it offers the possibility to combine the differrent transmission techniques in a common access architecture. The proposed solution is an extension of the APON system, an ATM based FITL system, as presented in Verbiest et al (1). In the first section, the generic functionality of today's access networks are discussed. Then the overall characteristics of the proposed (IBA are discussed, with the emphasis on the multiplexing functionality and the bandwidth flexibility. Single stage and multiple stage multiplexers are discussed. Finally, a number of applications are discussed, and conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: The common air interface (CAI) : the experience gained by France Telecom on three application fields of this european wireless network access standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: After an introduction to the ETSI Standard of the "Common Air Interface" for cordless communication, the present paper gives the example of the Telepoint network which FRANCE TELECOM has built up on the basis of this specification. This also presents the experience gained in operating such a new service.

articleTitle: A new approach to outside plant planning of the fiber feeder network in Bell Canada's Metropolitan core areas
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper outlines a new, outside plant, fundamental planning approach for the fiber cable feeder network in Bell Canada's metropolitan core areas (characterized by high-density development, extensive underground structures, and short loop lengths). The new approach, termed the Integrated Fiber Cable Network (IFCN) plan, uses Fiber Feeder Zones (FFZs) to plan and administer the fibers of all feeder cable architectures (single-path to dual central-office rings). The key characteristics of the IFCN and feeder administration are described. Supporting cost analysis is provided, as well as results from an application study within Bell Canada.

articleTitle: Access networks with route diversity: a planning approach and field evaluations
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The paper deals with the description of a flexible meshed optical fibres cabling structure, which allows increased network reliability for business users through double paths, dual hosting and dual homing functionalities. The main characteristics of the meshed structure, and related transmission architecture based on SDH equipment , are described; case studies have been carried out on a group of local office areas in Turin and results are presented from a technical and economic point of view, considering infrastructure, cabling and equipment costs.

articleTitle: Newly developed support system for subscriber optical fiber cable operations
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This article describes and evaluates the design and performance of a newly developed support system for subscriber optical fiber cable operations. The former support system, which was capable of automatic remote testing without any interruption in service, was introduced, and could decrease the amount of time for test work during cable construction by 75% and repair time by 50%. In addition to this feature, the new system allows one test controller to be shared by several offices, Moreover, carrier equipment faults are clearly separable from user equipment faults in the test results. Consequently, the application possibilities for the new support system increase along with the precision of identifying faults. Our evaluation of the new system's functions is based upon tests performed on a system prototype assembled specifically for this purpose.

articleTitle: Copper drop bandwidth capabilities
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper discusses bandwidth capabilities for existing telco drop and in-home twisted pair copper wiring. Bandwidth, group delay, cross-talk and EMI were measured in the DC-100 MHz range both in the lab and in the field. The results are applicable for broadband upgrades for Fiber-to-the-Curb systems. Service delivery options that result from this work are discussed, with particular emphasis on low cost transmission options, rather than ultimate information capacity.

articleTitle: Access modernization for next generation networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Owing to rapid technological advancements and deregulation in the telecommunications industry, Today's end-users have more service options to meet their business requirements. Telecommunication service providers are striving to meet their customers' increasing expectations in terms of service quality and price. To meet these challenges, telecommunications providers must continue to improve their operations environment by making best use of emerging technological advancements for both the network element and network management domains. This paper will describe how telecommunications service providers may optimize their operating environment based on end-customer service needs that provide the highest level of availability and lowest operating cost. In addition, results of several joint planning studies that have involved covering the considerable intelligence available in the emerging network technologies have shown that significant benefits, such as reductions in cycle time (90 percent), improved trouble report rates (60 percent), and expense reduction (50 percent), can be achieved.

articleTitle: System architecture for personal-id-based communication services
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: A personal communication network, which enables each user to communicate with any persol anywhere and at any time, is drawing special attention. Most studies of personal communications have focused on terminal mobility, using wireless interfaces and mobile terrninals, and there are few studies on how to realize personalized services according to each person's activity. This paper proposes a personal-IT based communication service and describes its basic functions and system architecture.

articleTitle: Bandwidth controllable ATM leased line services for private networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper proposes the high-speed ATM leased line services that can be constructed on the ATM transport system. Bandwidth controllability of the ATM system is the most significant feature in realizing these services for flexible and cost-effective private networks. Variable-bandwidth services and VPG(Virtual Path Group) service as optional services for ordinary (fixed) leased line services are discussed in this paper with reference to service specifications, potential applications and system configurations.

articleTitle: Intelligent network management systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper introduces model based reasoning techniques to the different applications within and at different levels of TMN. Fault management as one of the five FCAPS (Fault-, Configuration-, Accounting-, Performance- and Security Management) applications has been chosen for exemplary application of those techniques. Within a RACE (Research in Advanced Communications for Europe) project an implementation of model based reasoning has been developed and successfully applied to fault management of different existing networks, Future work will have to be performed to fully integrate and apply these concepts to all FCAPS areas for a fully automatic provisioning of TMN functionality.

articleTitle: An object-oriented operation system configuration for local optical fiber networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Operation systems need to be introduced into local optical fiber networks to rapidly respond to diversifying service demands and operation requirements. This paper deals with the introduction of object-oriented technologies for local optical fiber network operation systems. The proposed object-oriented system modeling will permit the most efficient establishment and management of local optical fiber networks. First, this paper briefly describes the basic configuration of local optical fiber networks and supporting operation systems. Next, functional assignments between operation systems are descdbed in terms of their "management domains", the latter being a concept found within the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) management framework developed in ISO. Finally, a mechanism that maintains the consistency of managed objects between various management domains is explained.

articleTitle: Fair bandwidth control in ATM-systems by artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper is part of a research project to examine the use of fuzzy controllers and artificial neural networks in the resource management of high speed networks. It deals with an investigation on adaptive flow-control mechanism based on artificial neural networks integrated in ATM networks. In addition to a new overall concept, two new methods for static and dynamic assignment of priorities for individual services or connections are presented. The results are verified by means of extensive simulations.

articleTitle: Multiple technologies in a single access platform
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Parallel development of DLC (Digital Loop Carrier) and FITL (Fiber-In-The-Loop) technologies and tbt introduction of SONET (Synchronous Optical NETwork) or SDH (Synchronous Digital Hierarchy) in the loo! have led many access system suppliers to develop new multi-functional network elements, which we refer to a Multiple Technologies Access Terminals (MTATs). Such MTATs may have a SONET interface on the feede side (supporting SONET transport to the wire center) and both fiber and copper terminations on the line side (supporting DLC and FITL applications). This is only one example of an MTAT but it is the focus of this paper because it is a real product of several suppliers and the issues associated with its appearance in the marketplace demand immediate attention. While each technology component of an MTAT may conform to the applicable generic requirements or public standards, there are cases where the appropriate requirements for a specific MTK configuration are unclear. The result is that MTAT products may not fully interoperate and may jeopardize Mix-and-match. This paper explores some of the technology specific conflicts, gaps or overlaps in requirements.

articleTitle: Future subscriber services - an architecture for rapid deployment
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper takes a radical review of the Standard method of provision of future subscriber services q, envisaged in the Intelligent Network concept and defined by CCITT and Bellcore. A long term architecture is proposed for the Intelligent Network which is both flexible and future-proof Such an architecture simplifies the customer access to the Intelligent Network for both service subscribers and service providers The constraints imposed by the Intelligent Network Capability Sets, or Releases, are removed. Therefore future subscriber services can be deployed without recourse to further switching network enhancements.

articleTitle: Value added fax network resources and services
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: First, this paper provides a presentation of Fax Value Added Services. Customer interfaces are described and discussed. Then an overview of the architecture of the France Telecom system and a description of the principles of call establishment is provided. The next part describes each sub-system and their main technical characteristics. FPAD performance and fax transmission on X.25 peculiarities are discussed. The last part proposes foreseeable paths for future evolution of Fax VAS, and the relative evolution of the dedicated equipments.

articleTitle: Impact of service requirements on radio network architecture and technology choice for PCS and wireless CAN
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The interest in the application of mobile radio technology to the Customer Access Network (CAN) i-increasing. This includes wireless distribution to fixed transceivers cabled to fixed phones as well as to portable stations, herein referred to as fixed access and portable access respectively. Also, the concept of the Personal Communications Service (PCS) is emerging with the aims of providing communication acces anywhere/anytime using a pocketable terminal together with a personal number and service profile [1] Considering the immense popularity of cellular and cordless phones, and the universality implied in PCS , it seems inevitable that radio in the CAN will not be considered separately from PCS, but rather as part of PCS Also, because of the diverse needs of communications users and the parallel development of several mobile equipment standards with the capability for supporting wireless access, the potential exists for both wireles: CAN and PCS to evolve from different technology platforms and with different architecture solutions. The most prominent are those evolving from the fixed and cellular networks, as illustrated in Fig. 1, herein referre-to as scenarios I and II respectively, and described below.

articleTitle: Radio in the local loop
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This is a general overview, presenting the advantages of using CT and DECT in the local loop. Aspects such as costs, network integration, different applications, new network solutions etc. will be covered. Experiences of narrowband measurement at 900 MHz (CT2 and CT3) have been carried out to evaluate the radio path losses between the transmitter and receiver. The results of these measurements, which indicated a range of up to 3 km in free space, are presented.

articleTitle: Services and applications of the BREHAT project
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: BREHAT is a French acronym which stands for'ATM high bit rate cross connect network. It is the name of a common project which has been led in association between CNET (the FRANCE TELECOM Research Laboratories), Alcatel-CIT and TRT-Philips. Its objective is to experiment and demonstrate the service integration capabilities of ATM. For that equipment and their related administration functions have been specified and developed, both for the public network and for the customer premises. This paper gives an overview of the project, focusing on the provided services both to the user and to the network operator.

articleTitle: Subnetwork management and TMN in an evolving network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: In today's dynamic telecommunications environment, change is occurring on many fronts. Services and network technologies are advancing rapidly, competition among service providers is intensifying, and customer demand for network access and customized services is increasing. This rapid pace of change is forcing operating telecommunications companies to streamline, simplify, and automate their network-management operations. The most effective means of achieving these objectives is through an evolution of the existing operations, administration and maintenance (OAM) architecture. This paper extends the Element Management Layer (EML) concept in CCITT Telecommunications Management Network (TMN) into sub-network management which will enable service providers to enhance service responsiveness and achieve their business objectives, such as reducing operations costs and capitalizing on new revenue-generating opportunities. Access and Integrated Switch-access clusters are used to demonstrate the concept of sub-network management in the evolving network.

articleTitle: Scenario-based usability assessment of ISDN terminals and resulting improvements
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: We describe a scenario-based procedure for usability assessment of ISDN feature terminals, demon strate its application to a typical terminal and discuss the resulting improvement of terminal design. The assessment is based on two scenarios which are created with regard to the user model.

articleTitle: Broadband hypermedia
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper describes ongoing work on integration of broadband services into a distributed hypermedia system. The services under consideration are video telephony, video conferencing, transfer of multimedia information and support for cooperative work. Milestones in the evolution of this system were: provision of a workstation based multimedia platform, adding capabilities for distributed data retrieval, implementation of basic hypermedia features and finally enhancement with broadband service components in order to support joint interactive working in a conferencing environment. This level of integration allows us to introduce the notion of broadband hypermedia. Realizations of the hypermedia prototype on networks using ATM-, MAN- and STM-technology are reported.

articleTitle: Communications maintenance at the crossroads
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Access Network maintenance is currently facing several challenges from technology changes and re-engineering of processes. The system infrastructure choices made in the next two years will determine how successfully Telecom Australia handles the widespread transition from a copper based Access Network to an electronic and fibre based network. This paper describes how Telecom Australia is developing the infrastructure and practices to make this transition. It also describes the rule based systems that have been used to analyse maintenance information and make maintenance recommendations.

articleTitle: Application-level flow control in the OSI management model
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Telecommunications operations have varying degrees of importance in maintaining high-quality service to telephone companies' customers. When Operations, Administration, Maintenance, and Provisioning (OAM&P) messages are implemented using the OSI model (CMIS/ROSE/ASN.1), the design requires the intelligence of an application-layer flow control rather than a "dumb" physical, data link, or network layer control. The main objective of this paper is to describe the flow control problem from an application perspective and show why a Layer 2-based flow control (which is currently used) is inadequate. A Network Traffic Management (NTM) model based flow control is suggested to manage end-to-end flow control at an application level.

articleTitle: A FITL system for deployment of optical fibers in germany (OPAL 93) - a basis for evolution of access networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: In the OPAL 93 project the Deutsche Bundespost Telekom (DBPT) installs FITL networks for approximately 200.000 subscribers. The SIEMENS solution with passive optical networks for interactive and broadband distributive services is presented with emphasis on some points of special interest. An outlook for evolution to an universal access network, allowing new approaches for network optimisation and future features, is given.

articleTitle: ATM advanced operation and management functions for B-ISDN
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: ATM transport networks will be constructed using the virtual path scheme. Virtual path OAM functions compare considered to enhance the ATM transport networks. Five virtual path OAM functions are proposed: maintenance signal transfer, testing, tracing, performance monitoring, and hitless line switching. The OAM cell drop and insert technique that does not interrupt live traffic is introduced, and the above OAM functions are realized in a prototype ATM transport system. Test results are also shown and the advantages of the VP OAM functions are verified.

articleTitle: Environment study for asymmetrical digital subscriber line in Taiwan
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The concept of Asymmetrical Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) is to provide greater than 1.544 Mbps DSI or higher bit rate service from the networking end to the customer end through the ordinary telephone line. For purpose of evaluating the performance of the ADSL within the local loop plant of Taiwan, we utilize quadrature amplitude modulation QAM) passband signaling scheme with 16 point constellation as an example for the present study. In this paper, we present the current loop plant environment and feasibility study of ADSL in Taiwan. The loop survey results show the crosstalk loss is around 10 dB and 15 dB, respectively, worse than the ANSI model. Preliminary simulation results show the transmission coverage range can be achieved at 17 kft for the FS PIC cable and 13.5 kft for the paper cable in the presence of self-FEXT (far-end crosstalk), background noise and up to 99 disturbers NEXT (near-end crosstalk) from Basic Rate DSL. ADSL coverage range can achieve a significant portion of the entire copper loop plant as sharing the same binder group with ISDN Basic Rate Access. Replacing NEXT from Basic Rate DSL by 10-disturber HDSL NEXT, the transmission range will be shorten to be 9.5 Ut and 6.5 kft for the FS PIC and paper cable, respectively. Hence, the engineering rule for HDSL installation should be carefully treated for the future deployment of ADSL in Taiwan's copper loop plant.

articleTitle: Designing architectures for optical access networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The introduction of fiber in the access network in The Netherlands is scheduled for the nearby futu, and preparations for it have already been started. A tool has been developed that plans several network architectures so that a cost effective and reliable architecture can be determined. The tool uses data, existing geographical situations as input.

articleTitle: SDH in the access network: Italy's approach to network and management issues
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper addresses Italys approach to the issue of telecommunications services provisioning in the flexible network environment that will be implemented with the introduction and full exploitation of SDH equipments. In particular it is focused on the impact that such SDH technology will have on the access network, in terms of increased flexibility for the fast and effective provision of services to the customer and increased reliability of the access network itself for the protection of customer traffic. In addition, the paper outlines the management requirements of such SDH environment, presenting the architecture of management systems specified for the efficient use of the available capacity and flexibility.

articleTitle: Impact of mobile communications technology on rural telecommunications
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Bringing high performance telecommunications systems to rural and suburban areas is a matter of strategic importance for their economic growth. Mobile communications technologies now make it possible to offer solutions appropriate to rural telecommunications requirements, on very favourable cost terms. This paper compares the available technologies, in terms of the functionalities they offer and their cost effectiveness, ISN before comprehensively analysing the 'CT2/CAI cordless technology', and describing the Tangara/RD system designed for subscriber radio access networks in rural and suburban areas.

articleTitle: Integrated services delivery multi-service delivery to major customer sites
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: BT's top 200 customers have 90,000 UK sites with more than a single line. By 1997, 1000 sites will require more than 34Mb/s access capacity: 80,000 sites will require up to 2Mb/s access capacity. Services to these customers are presently provided using a wide range of network platforrns and interfaces. Both in the UK and Globally, BT's customers will be looking for managed services and very high quality of service (QOS). Their expectation is that QOS for a particular service will be the same at any of their sites, large or small. In the UK, customers will be comparing our quality with the best-of-breed abroad, and the challenge is to deliver to this standard consistently and economically. The key characteristics of the market include geographically diffuse applications and immense diversity between and within customer networks. The current explosion in major customer demand for new service requirements shows no signs of slowing down and looks set to make ever wider demands on BT's network. Figure I illustrates some of the main features of service being considered. The basic requirement of our customers is to have traffic (voice, data, video, and high-bandwidth applications) transported from one point to another. On the way, the traffic may require a wide variety of treatments, some of them to meet the customer's application needs and some of them to ensure economic handling of the traffic. Treatments are combined and marketed as products. A modem network must therefore be a sophisticated managed, high quality transport network with access to "treatment facilities". The latter include digital exchanges, network control facilities for private circuits, Managed Bandwidth Service multiplexors and management, Advanced Services Units, and many others. Unless the basic transport network connecting the ten-ninal points of the customer's traffic is stable, error-free, resilient, and available on demand, effort spent on sophisticated treatments is largely wasted. Even a sophisticated service will be shunned by customers if it is unreliable.

articleTitle: Signaling models for control of B-ISDN and in-supported services
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper identifies a set of functional objectives for signaling architectures and protocols to support services in broadband and Intelligent Networks. Using a formal methodology called Object-Oriented Analysis, we define call, connection, and channel objects. Based on these object definitions and relationships, a need for separation of call and connection control in such networks is motivated. A multi-network functional architecture treating users as entities belonging in subscriber networks, and servers as entities separated from switches, is described. Service-specific client-server based protocols are identified as being well-suited for inter-entity communication in this architecture.

articleTitle: Giving customers choice in visual services
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Although new networks such as ISDN provide enormous potential for high quality services and applications, very little of this potential has been used to date. The complexities of network connection alone are enough to scare off most potential users and developers. This paper describes a trial value-added network service being developed by Telstra which allows easy use cf telecommunications networks for a wide range of visual services-without subscribers or information providers needing detailed knowledge of network technology.

articleTitle: Wireless connection using mm-waves and fibre
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: There is considerable interest and application potential in judiciously combining optical fibre and microwave/ mm-wave radio technology to effect efficient delivery of wireless telecommunication services. This paper explores the application of advanced optical fibre technology to the generation, and delivery to a remote antenna site, of mm-wave signals for future mobile radio and other wireless access services. The particular approach discussed deals also with the provision of a return link, utilising the same fibre as used for the forward link, from the antenna site to the base station to enable fun-duplex operation. The paper begins by outlining the need for such systems, stressing in particular the expected increase in demand for access to broadband services from a mobile or remote terminal. A description of the topology of a specific system demonstrator under development within the RACE programme is provided. This is followed by a discussion of some possible system applications, focusing in particular on the system's applicability to mobile telecommunications and the provision of telecommunication services to remote communities. The technology developed during this research project will allow the development of future standards for the definition of the interconnect between the fixed network and a mobile/remote user environment. The paper seeks also to expose broadband networks and services specialists to the capabilities of this emerging technology with a view to fostering its take up and exploitation. It is hoped that this may help to promote dialogue between the 'base technology' and the 'networks and system architectures' communities to ensure that the flexibility offered by this broadband deployment option is considered in future standards setting decisions.

articleTitle: Open distributed management of telecom systems: the missing link
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper presents an architecture for a distributed open management system. After a discussion of current deficiencies of the ISO OSI information model for manaoement information structure, we will introduce the "Missing Link", a distributed information layer as an extension of the standard. The consequences for the manager-agent model will be outlined as well as the possibilities one gains with the new model. Next the achievements of the DOMAINS project will be discussed which developed a information structuring model on a distributed object oriented approach. Both the Domains Management Architecture (DMA)and the Object-Oriented Architecture (OOA) can be ported to different platforms. This enables real open distributed management.

articleTitle: Service design and human factors considerations in the introduction of personal communications services
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Rapid advancements in telecommunications technologies are opening many new opportunities to broaden a service provider's customer base, and offer those customers more choices in order to personalize services. The advent of intelligent network technology design concepts allows rapid service introduction based on customer needs and the flexibility to personalize a service to an individual's needs through the Intelligent Network's Service Creation Environmentl. However, as Southwestern Bell's Personal Communications service design work has shown, the ability to offer robust, flexible, and personalized services is limited by the resulting complexity of the service and the customer's ability to easily understand how the service operates. We are faced with the following dilemma: How can we offer services with enough flexibility to meet a wide range of customers' needs while ensuring that any one customer is not inundated with too many features? This is an important issue since customers will not use - and therefore not pay for - services which they perceive to be too complex. This paper describes Southwestern Bell's first attempt to provide Personal Communications services using the robust capabilities of an intelligent network platforms. We examine how the service design process was conducted (using the axiom that services must be driven by your Marketing organization and not your technology organization), what we learned, and how we will improve our methodology in future endeavors. The implications of using a service prototyping platform are also discussed.

articleTitle: The DECT potential in the local loop
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper describes the DECT standard and radio Interface and provides Information on the DECT application areas, especially in the local loop. Results of propagation measurements are also presented.

articleTitle: The global information trading environment
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper discusses the architectural nature of an "Information Trading Environment" and how it evolves from the current communications architectures. It also discusses some of the elements and components which will evolve to provide user interaction with such an environment, and some of the possible implications of information trading on a global scale in virtual environments.

articleTitle: Future communication services in the automotive industry
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The complexity of today's industrial application software, and the distributed nature of those industries is placing an increasing demand on both local and wide area networks. Because of this it is essential that we investigate and specify the network service requirements of such industries, to ensure that the evolving broadband networks will meet their needs. This paper summarises and describes the service requirements of the automotive industry as identifled by RACE project CAR.

articleTitle: "Status report and prospects on optical distribution in France"
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The use of optical fibres in the distribution network brings with it significant service benefits for users including improved transmission quality, access protection facilities and open-endedness to accommodate changing requirements. This is why, after running tests on three sites in Greater Paris, FRANCE TELECOM has begun a nationwide programme to provide flexible optical access networks (Optical FAS) for its biggest customers, serving central business district buildings requiring more than four 2 Mbit/s links. For smaller businesses, with requirements ranging from to one to six 2 Mbit/s links, shared fibre systems have been on trial. Additional trials will be needed before taking a final decision as to the viability of residential connections. This article describes the current situation in France and the initial results obtained from business networks.

articleTitle: What are the traffic characteristics of the emerging distributed multimedia communication services?
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The paper reports on experiences from experiments with novel interactive multimedia communication services. New user interfaces open up for entirely new ways to communicate and give rise to new traffic patterns. We focus on description of the some applications and discuss our plans to explore their traffic characteristics and their implications for Quality of Service requirements on underlying networks.

articleTitle: Reliability guidelines for the deployment of SONET rings in the feeder network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper describes some deployment factors that could affect the reliability of SONET rings in the feeder network. The reliability effects of equipment and cable failure rates and repair times are quantified and used to show how reliability changes with ring size, bit rate and location of a node on the ring. Procedural and software errors are briefly considered, and it is recommended that field performance be monitored to determine if actual performance approaches that predicted by the models.

articleTitle: Application of high bit-rate digital subscriber line (HDSL) technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: High bit-rate Digital Subscriber Line (HDSL) technology permits two-way 1.544 or 2.048 Mb/s transport over most existing copper telephone cables without repeaters, cable conditioning, or binder group segregation. Approximately 1000 HDSLs are now in service, and the rate of deployment is accelerating. Compared with traditional high speed copper transport systems, HDSL engineering, installation, and maintenance are simpler. Non-intrusive measurement of Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and digital performance greatly improves the HDSL's utility. HDSL permits rapid and low-cost service turn-up for private line DS1, fractional DSI rate, switched services, and access to PCS base stations. A strong synergy exists between HDSL and the fiber deployments planned for the next several years.

articleTitle: Application of TMN principles to ATM networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The international normalization body CCITT has defined a global model for the management of telecommunication networks and services, called the TMN. This paper shows how a new technique, the asynchronous transfer mode, greatly benefits from this work.

articleTitle: Flexible wideband services to the residence: service architectures to meet customer demand
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) technology offers capabilities that can provide access to flexible wideband services, while using the large installed base of copper loops. The market for these services and the status of ADSL standards work are discussed; and some alternatives for ADSL protocols, focusing on OSI layer 2, are considered and compared.

articleTitle: Allocation of functionality in flexible access networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The increased demand for telecommunication services, both in volume and diversity, encourage telecommunication administrations to install flexible access networks. A flexible access network, based on the newest technology (e.g., fiber transmission systems, software controiled access nodes) makes it possible to provide a broad range of subscriber interfaces and services. Modern operations systems will automate the provisioning and maintenance processes to a large extent, reducing the time to introduce and begin providing a service. A flexible access network requires standard interfaces to the rest of the telecommunications network and the operations systems. A new approach to the allocation of functions among the network elements of the access network and the rest of the telecommunications network is required to obtain a useful interface specification.

articleTitle: A copper/fiber access evolution for video dial tone delivery
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper discusses the continuing use of copper facilities, with appropriate electronics, to provide Video Dial Tone services to residential customers. The technological and econornic basis for this capability will be described in the context of a practical transition to a fiber-based access network. The goal is to leverage the embedded copper network during this transition period, to begin offering new video and multimedia services cost effectively before fiber is widely deployed. Economic modeling of the distribution plant shows that use of embedded copper distribution facilities is well suited to supporting early low-penetration demand for new video services.

articleTitle: The subscriber access - the most complex challenge network operators ever met
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: The development in the field of telecommunication networks has arrived at a crossroads. In the past the transmission network consisted of largely independent components such as multiplexers, line equipment, regenerators, network terminations etc, which interworked via internationally standardized interfaces and could be specified and operated as individual components due to the simplicity of structures.

articleTitle: Powering options for fiber-in-the-loop systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: A key challenge remaining to ubiquitous fiber-in-the-loop deployment is powering. Of particular concern is now best to power optical network units (ONU), which provide the interface between the loop fiber and customer drop wires. Currently, two basic ONU-powering schemes have been defined. In this paper, we examine several variations to these schemes. These include the use of new battery technologies as backup sources, solar photovoltaic power as a primary source, and fiber as a power transmission medium. We also support new information on ac power quality in the United States and on power system hardware reliability, and ow these effect the overall availability of the subscriber loop.

articleTitle: From copper to fiber in the Italian loop network architectures, economics, deployment strategies
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: This paper deals with the modernization of the Italian access network and in particular with the introduction of optical technologies into the subscriber loop plant. An overview is presented of the chosen network architecture and the pursued evolution approach, as based on strategic motivations, available technologies and relevant cost profiles. the economics of the copper-to-fiber transition is also addressed, and the short-mid term deployment steps are outlined.

articleTitle: Access network - choices and organisational environments in india
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Today's Telecommunications environment is changing at a much greater rate because of rapidly evolving capabilities of technology. Another driving force is the demand for increasingly broad range of services and for greater integration of those services. There is also an increasing awareness in Telecommunication administration that there is no functional difference between a Regional Telecom Network and Rural Net work in terms of required services. Subscribers' demands in rural areas for the enhanced services (voice, data etc.) equivalent to their counterparts in Metro areas are increasing. Inspite of all these changes, majority of customer access is still limited to plain old telephony service which represents major segment of traffic to be carried, especially in rural network. India with 600,000 villages and with a population of 858 million, thus faces a major challenge in restructuring telecommunication services to meet customers' demands for superior services on growing scale. This paper discusses Indian environment and appropriateness of technology for the required conditions to provide access to the rural areas for basic telephone and information transfer facilities. It focusses also on the access architecture for a total network solution with hostlremote switches and transmission systems to provide better accessibility and services in urban areas.

articleTitle: BARBARA: using advanced telecommunications to bring customer services to rural areas
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Throughout Europe the services and facilities available to people in urban areas are generally far superior to those in the rural areas. The gap between these areas is continually widening with the consequent movement of more and more people from the rural areas into the towns. This drift increases the strain on already overloaded services and infrastructures. Advanced communications could, if concentrated in the cities and within large businesses, further encourage this trend. The BARBARA (Broad Range of Community Based Telecommunications Applications in Rural Areas ) Project is about trying to reverse some of these trends and to improve the quality of life of people in the remote areas of the Highlands. The project has set out to provide a broad range of practical applications which will be of benefit to remote rural areas by the use of ISDN (integrated Services Digital Network ) and to later look at the practicality of migrating the services to Broadband (2 megabit/s) The project is also about meeting the needs of real users living and working in remote rural communities so a major part of the project has been concerned with the research into the requirements of the users and providers of the service in the rural communities as much as the technical aspects of how the advance telecommunications and multimedia technology could be developed. The objectives of the research have been to determine the services which will be of practical value and which could be realistically provided. The success or failure of the project is to be judged on the extent to which it delivers services which the rural communities use. Though the Barbara project is a European funded project under the RACE programme we will only be describing the work carried out in the Highland Region for the Highland Regional Council in conjunction with BT.

articleTitle: Advanced evaluation method for strategic investment in network evolution
publicationTitle: Proceedings. The X International Symposium on Subscriber Loops and Services,
abstract: Telecommunication services are expected to be upgraded from POTS (plain old telephone service) to N-ISDN/B-ISDN services in the near future, requiring deployment of optical fibers in subscriber loops. Local exchange carriers have to invest a huge amount of money in installing optical fibers and equipment, so investment strategy should be based on evaluation of various possible network evolutions from an economic viewpoint. In planning the investment strategy for network upgrading, which new technology to use and the investment timing for upgrading the existing network should be determined simultaneously. This paper proposes an advanced method for evaluating investment strategies for network upgrading. Parameters that influence the investment strategy are analyzed for N-ISDN and B-ISDN services.
